title: PixelKin - Wild Battle (Dusk Duel)
_note: The default wild-encounter theme (also the attract-mode trailer duel). Same first-principles excitement toolkit as the heroic title, but tuned for IN-THE-FIGHT urgency - faster and more relentless than the title (the title previews this; this IS the fight). Devices: A natural minor (Aeolian) with i-bVI-bVII motion and a HARMONIC-MINOR dominant (E, raised G# leading tone) for tension; a busy, SYNCOPATED, LEAPING saw lead with chromatic neighbours; a relentless PUMPING root-fifth eighth-note bass (a chase, never resting); a driving pulse arpeggio; hard battle drums; and brass that stabs through the tense A-section then SUSTAINS through a heroic C-major B-lift (the anthemic C-G-Am-F) so a random fight feels exciting and winnable, not scary. Climbs to a high C6 climax, then an E-dominant cadence slams the loop back to Am. 158 BPM, A minor, 16-bar loop (~24s). Cohesive with the title (shared A-minor heroic palette: saw lead + brass + galloping/pumping low end). Vesper rising-leap appears fragmented per the score's battle treatment. Renders on the chip engine for cohesion. Original melody throughout (VISION.md).
key: A minor (Aeolian + harmonic-minor dominant), lifting to C major

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: Urgent, syncopated, leaping - a battle riff, not a melody you'd hum a child to sleep with. A (bars 1-8): a restless A-minor hook over the i-bVI-bVII-iv-V motion, off-beat accents, chromatic G# at the E cadence. B (bars 9-16): lifts into a heroic C-major answer (the 'you can win this' payoff), climbing to a high C6 climax, then an E-major (G#) cadence that pulls the loop back to A.

tracks.name: drums
tracks._note: Hard driving battle beat: kick on 1 & 3 with a push on the 'and of 3', snare on 2 & 4, hats on the eighths. Crash opens each section; tom fills close each 8-bar half. Each bar = 8 eighths.
